newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH KOC, FIAT DISCUSS TOFAS.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH KOC, FIAT DISCUSS TOFAS.

text.p: Turkey's Koc Holding and Italian Fiat Spa are discussing plans for car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi, said Koc Holding, the country's leading industrial group in a statement sent to the Istanbul stock exchange.
The two companies were discussing investment and production plans, the development of exports, new models and management planning in their Tofas joint-venture, Koc Holding said.
Discussions were also covering an option system for the sale of shares to one another after a four-year period, Koc Holding said.
But it said short-term sale of shares was not being considered by either party.
Koc and Fiat each hold a 37.86 percent stake in Tofas, which accounts for around 50 percent of Turkish car production.
Activity in Koc Holding and Tofas shares have recently enlivened on the Istanbul stock market on rumours that Koc may sell its Tofas stake to Fiat.
In an October 10 statement released because of the rumours, Koc Holding said it, in the short term, was not considering selling its Tofas stake to Fiat.
Tofas has stopped production several times this year in the face of slack demand.

It reduced production to single shift from two on December 2 after capacity usage at its Bursa plant fell below 40 percent and decided to lay off 1,011 workers, or 22 percent of its workforce from January 2, 1997, because of a further slump in sales on anticipation of cheaper car imports.
The government developed a scheme to allow a limited number of duty free car imports from June 1997 by Turkish expatriates and residents who deposit at least 50,000 marks at a state bank by end-1996.
